story.see: The same Tonle Sap season, 19 June to 17 October, run again on calibrated full-resolution radar data instead of the preview images. The detail is finer: river channels stay continuous and the map shows 773 separate water bodies where the preview map showed 344. Open water grows from about 2,300 square kilometres in June to about 5,600 on 17 October.
story.physics: Calibrated data give the real radar backscatter in decibels, so the thresholds are physical numbers. On 17 October they give about 5,600 square kilometres of open water, against about 5,000 from the preview images and about 5,400 from an independent estimate based on the lake-level altimeter and 38 years of Landsat. Averaged over the ten passes the result is within about 6 percent of that estimate; the preview detector was off by 20 percent.
story.lband: Calm water is very dark to the L-band radar, and rough water is brighter, so wind on 18 August shrinks the mapped lake. Water under flooded trees and shrubs is harder to see: the flooded-vegetation layer marks possible cases, and the true area under the canopy is uncertain by about a factor of 1.5.
story.people: Honest limits: the calibration is still PROVISIONAL. The thresholds were tuned on this scene, and the same thresholds do not work at Lake Sevan, which was imaged in another radar mode. Treat the numbers as a careful measurement of this season, not a finished product.
